newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal prices bullish on limited supplies.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal prices bullish on limited supplies.

text.p: Indian soymeal prices remained bullish during the week on limited soybean arrivals and good export demand, traders said on Tuesday.

Traders said soymeal was quoted at $321-322 per tonne fas (free alongside ship) at west coast ports, compared with $230 at the same time last year. They added prices could go up further due to low capacity utilisation.

"Capacity utilisation was around 12 to 15 percent against the normal 40 percent. Capacity utilisation may further decrease as avaialbility of raw material was very poor," said Sandeep Agrawal, a senior official of Gujrat Ambuja Protein Ltd.
Agrawal said Indian soymeal was in good demand due to its high 48 percent protein content, compared with 44-46 percent in soymeal of other origins.
Traders said daily soybean arrivals were around 800 tonnes in the central Indian markets compared with about 12,000 tonnes per day at the same time last year.
In thin trading soybean was quoted at 13,200-13,400 rupees per tonne compared with 11,100-11,350 rupees a year earlier.
Traders said Indian rapeseed extraction was also in good demand and quoted at $121-122 per tonne fas in bulk.
